contents.html_ja: 国家安全保障局が 1986 年に開始したセキュアデータネットワークシステム（Secure Data Network System、SDNS）プロジェクトは、国際標準化機構（ISO）の開放型システム間相互接続（OSI）参照モデルの枠組みの中で、コンピュータネットワークのセキュリティアーキテクチャを生み出しました。第 4 層のセキュリティプロトコル（SP4）は、OSI 参照モデルのトランスポート層でセキュリティサービスを提供するために使われる、SDNS アーキテクチャの構成要素の一つです。本報告書は、SP4 のプロトコル実装適合性記述書（PICS）プロフォーマを規定します。SP4 の実装について PICS プロフォーマに記入すると、能力に関する明確で簡潔な記述が得られ、その実装の製造、試験、供給、調達、適用に関わるさまざまな状況で、関係者の役に立ちます。
contents.html: The Secure Data Network System (SDNS) project, initiated by the National Security Agency in 1986, produced a computer network security architecture within the framework of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) reference model for Open Systems Interconnection (OSI). The security protocol at layer 4 (SP4) is one element of the SDNS architecture used to provide security services at the Transport Layer of the OSI reference model. This report specifies the Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement (PICS) proforma for SP4. When the PICS proforma is completed for an SP4 implementation, it provides a clear and concise statement of capabilities, useful in a variety of situations to those involved in the production, testing, supply, procurement, and application of the implementation.

contents.html_ja: 米国国立標準技術研究所（NIST）と国家安全保障局（NSA）は、1984 年にコンピュータネットワークセキュリティに関する共同プロジェクトを開始しました。このプロジェクトは、地理的に分散したコンピュータネットワークにおいて、データへの費用対効果の高いアクセス制御を提供するには、包括的なセキュリティ機構一式が必要であるという認識に基づいていました。詳細なセキュリティ機構は、セキュリティを必要とする機密区分のある分野と機密区分のない分野とで異なる場合がありますが、共通のセキュリティアーキテクチャで商用コンピュータネットワークが開発されれば、どちらの分野にも利益があります。NSA は、少なくとも一部は、この共同プロジェクトの結果として、1986 年にセキュアデータネットワークシステム（SDNS）計画を開始しました。
contents.html: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the National Security Agency (NSA) initiated a joint project in Computer Network Security in 1984. The project was based on the recognition that a comprehensive set of security mechanisms is needed to provide cost effective access control to data in geographically distributed computer networks. While the detailed security mechanisms can differ between the classified and unclassified communities requiring security, both communities benefit when commercial computer networks are developed with a common security architecture. The NSA initiated the Secure Data Network System (SDNS) program in 1986 as a result, at least partially, of this joint project.

contents.html_ja: PICS プロフォーマの最初の部分である実装識別には、供給者と実装の両方を完全に識別するために必要な情報を、指示に従って記入します。PICS プロフォーマの主要部分は、小項に分かれた固定書式の質問票であり、各小項には個別の項目群が含まれます。質問票の項目への回答は、一番右の列に記入します。限定された選択肢（通常は「Yes」または「No」）を示す回答に印を付けるか、値、値の集合、または値の範囲を入力します。可能な回答の集合から2つ以上の選択肢が当てはまる項目もあります。そのため、該当するすべての選択肢に印を付けます。
contents.html: The first part of the PICS proforma, the Implementation Identification, is to be completed as indicated with the information necessary to identify fully both the supplier and the implementation. The main part of the PICS proforma is a fixed-format questionnaire divided into subclauses, each containing a group of individual items. Answers to the questionnaire items are to be provided in the rightmost column, either by simply marking an answer to indicate a restricted choice (usually "Yes" or "No"), or by entering a value or a set or range of values. Note that there are some items where two or more choices from a set of possible answers can apply. Therefore, all relevant choices are to be marked.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the National Security Agency (NSA) initiated a joint project in Computer Network Security in 1984. The project was based on the recognition that a comprehensive set of security mechanisms is needed to provide cost effective access control to data in geographically distributed computer networks. While the detailed security mechanisms can differ between the classified and unclassified communities requiring security, both communities benefit when commercial computer networks are developed with a common security architecture. The NSA initiated the Secure Data Network System (SDNS) program in 1986 as a result, at
least partially, of this joint project.

Security Protocol 4 (SP4) [1,2] is one element of the SDNS architecture [3], used to provide security services at the Transport Layer of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) Basic Reference Model (BRM) for Open System Interconnection (OSI) [4]. SP4 consists of a simple encapsulation/decapsulation protocol that protects normal Transport Protocol data units within a cryptographically secure envelope. SP4 is

This report specifies the Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement (PICS) proforma for SP4. The supplier of a protocol implementation which is claimed to conform to the SDNS Standard [1] shall complete the SP4 PICS proforma. A completed PICS proforma becomes the PICS for the implementation in question. The PICS is a statement identifying the capabilities and options of the protocol that have been
implemented. The PICS can serve a number of purposes, including as:
(1) a check list for the protocol implementer, to reduce the risk of failure to
conform to the standard through oversight;

The remainder of this report defines the procedures, format, and content that comprise the SP4 PICS proforma. The format is intended to follow the style used in the PICS proforma for the transport protocol [9]. Most of the content is derived directly
from the SP4 standard [1]. Appendix provides the rationale behind the content selection and explores the relationships between services, protocol, and functions.

APPENDIX A: SERVICE, FUNCTION, AND PROTOCOL RELATIONSHIPS

The SP4 standard poses a bit of a paradox. Its presentation is simple, yet a high degree of complexity arises when considering its use with the connectionless Transport protocol and the various classes of the connection oriented Transport protocol, in light of the available options. This complexity becomes more evident in the PICS proforma, since the full capabilities of the protocol must be expressed. Perhaps the hardest area of the proforma to reconcile is the SP4 service elements. This is due in large part to the somewhat weak service elements definitions appearing in the security addendum to the OSI reference model. The following guidelines are provided as an aid to understanding:
(1) Connection confidentiality is indicated when the Transport service is connection oriented and the TPDUs are protected accordingly.
(2) Connectionless confidentiality is indicated when the Transport service is connectionless and the TPDUs are protected accordingly.
